merge.title: Merge PDF – Combine PDF Files Online Free, No Upload | {brand}
merge.desc: Merge PDF files into one document in seconds. Free, no sign-up, no file limits and no watermark. Files are combined in your browser and never uploaded.

guide.intro: Merging PDFs is the quickest way to turn scattered documents – scans, invoices, chapters, forms – into one tidy file that is easy to share, print and archive. {brand} joins your files right inside your browser, so even confidential contracts or ID scans never touch a server.
uses: Combine a scanned passport, ID and application form into one PDF for an online application.
Join monthly invoices or bank statements into a single file for your accountant.
Put together chapters, a cover page and an appendix into one report or thesis.
Merge several signed pages back into the full contract.
tips: Sort files into the right order before you click Start – use the Up/Down buttons.
If the final file is too large for email, run it through Compress PDF afterwards.
Need only some pages from each file? Split or Extract pages first, then merge.

faq.q: Will merging reduce the quality of my PDFs?
faq.a: No. Pages are copied as they are, so text stays selectable and images keep their original quality.
Unlock them first with Unlock PDF (you need the password), then merge.

compress.title: Compress PDF – Reduce PDF File Size Online Free | {brand}
compress.desc: Compress PDF to reduce file size for email, WhatsApp and upload portals. Free, no limits, no sign-up – your PDF is compressed in your browser, never uploaded.

guide.intro: Large PDFs are rejected by email (often 20–25 MB limits) and by many government, job and college portals that accept only 1–2 MB. {brand} shrinks PDFs on your own device, so you can compress private documents without uploading them anywhere.
uses: Make a scanned PDF small enough for an online form with a 1 MB or 2 MB limit.
Send a large report by email or WhatsApp.
Save storage space on your phone or cloud drive.
tips: Try Lossless first – it keeps text selectable. Use Strong for scanned or photo-heavy files.
For text-based PDFs that are already small, large savings may not be possible.
Compress after merging, not before, to get one optimised file.

faq.q: How much smaller will my PDF be?
faq.a: It depends on the content. Scanned and image-heavy PDFs often shrink by 50–90% in Strong mode; text-only PDFs shrink less.

faq.q: Can I compress a PDF to under 1 MB or 100 KB?
faq.a: Often yes for scans using Strong mode. Very long documents may still be larger; splitting them can help.

split.title: Split PDF – Extract Pages or Split by Range Online Free | {brand}
split.desc: Split a PDF into single pages or custom ranges like 1-3,5. Free, unlimited and private – your PDF is split in your browser and never uploaded.

guide.intro: Splitting lets you pull out just the pages you need – one chapter, one invoice, one signed page – instead of sending a whole document. With {brand} the split happens locally, so large or sensitive PDFs stay on your device.
uses: Send only the relevant pages of a long contract or report.
Break a scanned bundle of receipts into one file per page.
Separate chapters of an e-book or study material.
tips: Use ranges like 1-3,7,10-12 to create several files at once.
Leave the field empty to split every page into its own PDF.
Want one file with chosen pages only? Use Extract pages instead.

faq.q: Will the split pages keep links and quality?
faq.a: Yes. Pages are copied without re-rendering, so text, images and quality are unchanged.

pdf2word.title: PDF to Word Converter – Convert PDF to DOCX Free | {brand}
pdf2word.desc: Convert PDF to an editable Word (DOCX) file for free. No sign-up, no limits, and your document is converted in your browser, never uploaded.

guide.intro: Converting a PDF to Word lets you reuse and edit the text in Microsoft Word, Google Docs or LibreOffice. {brand} extracts the text of each page into a DOCX file directly on your device. It works best for text-based PDFs such as letters, articles and reports.
uses: Reuse text from an old report or letter without retyping.
Edit a document when you no longer have the original Word file.
Copy paragraphs into a new document or presentation.
tips: This beta focuses on text; complex tables, columns and images may need manual touch-up.
Scanned PDF? Built-in OCR (Auto mode) reads pages that have no text layer.
If you only need plain text, PDF to Text is even faster.

faq.q: Can I open the result in Google Docs?
faq.a: Yes. DOCX files open in Microsoft Word, Google Docs, LibreOffice and WPS Office.
The converter extracts text paragraphs page by page, with OCR for scanned pages. Complex layouts, tables and images are not yet fully preserved.

jpg2pdf.title: JPG to PDF – Convert Images to PDF Online Free | {brand}
jpg2pdf.desc: Convert JPG, PNG and WebP images to one PDF. Choose page size and margins. Free, no watermark, no upload – images are converted in your browser.

guide.intro: Turning photos into a PDF is the easiest way to submit documents, homework or receipts as a single file. {brand} builds the PDF on your phone or computer, so personal photos and ID scans are never uploaded.
uses: Turn phone photos of documents into one PDF for an application.
Combine receipts into a PDF for expense claims.
Send homework or handwritten notes as a single file.
tips: Choose A4 or Letter page size for documents that will be printed.
Rotate or crop photos first with the image tools for a neater result.
If the PDF is too big, use Compress PDF afterwards.

faq.q: Can I convert many images at once?
faq.a: Yes. Select as many images as you like; each becomes a page in one PDF, in the order you choose.

guide.intro: Converting PDF pages to images makes them easy to share on social media, insert into slides or view on any device. {brand} renders each page in your browser at the resolution you choose.
uses: Share a single page of a PDF on WhatsApp or Instagram.
Insert PDF pages into PowerPoint or Google Slides.
Create thumbnails or previews of a document.
tips: Choose PNG for sharp text and diagrams, JPG for smaller photo pages.
Use 2x or 3x resolution if the images will be printed or zoomed.
more: JPG or PNG?

JPG gives smaller files for pages with photos. PNG keeps text and line art perfectly sharp and supports lossless quality. For screenshots of documents shared in chats, PNG at 2x is usually the best balance.
Resolution guide
1x is good for previews, 2x for most screens and documents, 3x for printing or zooming into details.

guide.intro: PDF keeps your document looking the same on every device, which is why most forms and portals ask for it. {brand} converts DOCX files to PDF inside your browser, so CVs and letters never leave your device.
uses: Turn your CV or cover letter into a PDF before applying for jobs.
Send letters or reports that must not be edited.
Prepare documents for printing.
tips: This beta keeps text, headings, bold, italic and lists; check documents with images or complex layout.
For full-fidelity layout, Word's own Save as PDF is also an option.
more: Why send PDF instead of Word

Word documents can look different on another computer because of missing fonts or different software versions. A PDF preserves the layout, is harder to modify accidentally and is accepted by virtually every job portal and organisation.
Compatibility
DOCX files from Microsoft Word, Google Docs (downloaded as DOCX), LibreOffice and Pages exports are supported.

guide.intro: Need to fill in a field, fix a typo or add a note to a PDF? {brand} lets you add text and white-out boxes on any page without installing software or uploading your file.
uses: Fill in a simple form that has no fillable fields.
Cover a mistake with white-out and type the correct text.
Add a date, name or note to a document.
tips: Zoom the preview to place text precisely.
To hide sensitive information permanently, use Redact PDF instead of white-out.
more: What you can edit

Add new text anywhere – names, dates, notes, answers on forms – choose its size and colour, and cover unwanted content with white-out boxes. It is ideal for quick fixes when you do not have the original document.
Limitations
Existing text is not directly editable; cover it and type over it. For permanent removal of sensitive information, use Redact PDF.

guide.intro: Sign documents in under a minute without printing and scanning. Draw your signature with a finger, mouse or stylus, or type it, and place it anywhere on the page – all on your device.
uses: Sign rental agreements, offer letters and consent forms.
Approve invoices or delivery notes.
Add initials to every page of a contract.
tips: Draw slowly on a phone for a smoother signature.
After signing, use Flatten PDF so the signature cannot be moved.
more: Electronic signatures

Visual e-signatures are widely accepted for everyday agreements in many countries. Some documents, such as certain legal or government filings, may require certificate-based digital signatures – check local rules when in doubt.
Signing on a phone
Draw your signature with a finger, place it on the right page and resize it to fit the signature line.

guide.intro: Adding a password stops anyone without it from opening your PDF. {brand} encrypts files with AES-256 locally, so neither the file nor the password is ever sent over the internet.
uses: Email salary slips, bank statements or medical reports safely.
Share ID documents with a password sent separately.
Protect business proposals and contracts.
tips: Use a long password – try our Password Generator.
Share the password through a different channel than the file.
more: How PDF encryption works

AES-256 is the strongest encryption defined in the PDF standard and is supported by Adobe Reader, Chrome, Edge, Firefox, macOS Preview and modern mobile viewers. Without the password, the content cannot be read.
Choosing a strong password
Use at least 12–16 characters mixing words, numbers and symbols. A passphrase like “Coffee-Window-42-Orbit” is both strong and memorable. Never send the password in the same email as the file.
Works offline
Encryption happens in your browser, so you can protect files even without an internet connection once the page has loaded.

guide.intro: Bank statements and e-bills often arrive password-protected. If you know the password, {brand} can remove it so you can open, print or merge the file freely – done locally in your browser.
uses: Remove the password from bank or credit-card statements you own.
Prepare protected PDFs for merging or compressing.
tips: You must know the password; this tool does not crack passwords.
more: Owner vs user passwords

PDFs can have an open password (needed to view) and permissions passwords that restrict printing, copying or editing. When you know the password, unlocking removes the protection so you can work with the file normally.
Legal and safe use
Only unlock documents you own or are authorised to access, such as your own bank statements, utility bills or payslips. After unlocking, store the file securely – it no longer has protection.
After unlocking
Once the password is removed, you can merge the file with other documents, compress it, add page numbers or print it without being asked for the password each time.

guide.intro: Scans and phone photos often end up sideways or upside down. Rotate PDF fixes the orientation permanently so the file opens correctly everywhere.
uses: Fix sideways scanned pages.
Turn landscape pages for easier reading.
tips: To rotate only some pages, use Organize PDF.
more: Rotating vs re-scanning

Re-scanning a sideways document wastes time and can reduce quality. Rotating a PDF only changes the page orientation instruction stored in the file, so text, images and file size stay exactly the same. The result opens correctly in Adobe Reader, browsers, Preview, phone viewers and printers.
Mixed orientations
Reports often mix portrait text pages with landscape tables or charts. Rotate only the landscape pages with Organize PDF so each page reads naturally on screen, then print with “auto-rotate” enabled.
Batch rotation
Select several PDFs at once and apply the same rotation to all of them – useful when a scanner fed a whole stack of pages in the wrong orientation.

guide.intro: Organize PDF shows every page as a thumbnail so you can reorder, rotate and delete pages visually – ideal for fixing scanned bundles.
uses: Fix pages scanned in the wrong order.
Remove blank or duplicate pages.
tips: On mobile use the arrow buttons on each thumbnail.
more: One tool for page clean-up
Instead of using separate tools to rotate, delete and reorder pages, Organize PDF shows the whole document as a page grid. Make all changes at once and export a single clean PDF.
Typical clean-up workflow
Scan a batch of documents, delete blank pages, rotate sideways ones, drag pages into order and export. Then compress the result if you need to email it.
Works on any device
Thumbnails are generated in your browser, so even large PDFs can be reorganised on a laptop, tablet or phone without uploading them to a server.

pagenumbers.title: Add Page Numbers to PDF Online Free – Custom Position & Start | {brand}
pagenumbers.desc: Number the pages of any PDF: choose position, font size and starting number. Free, no watermark, no sign-up – numbering happens in your browser.

guide.intro: Page numbers make long documents easier to navigate, cite and print – reviewers can say "see page 14" instead of scrolling. {brand} stamps numbers directly onto each page on your own device, so manuscripts, legal bundles and reports stay private.
uses: Number a thesis, dissertation or manuscript before submission.
Prepare court bundles or contract exhibits that must be referenced by page.
Add numbers to a merged report so readers can follow the table of contents.
Number printed handouts so loose pages can be put back in order.
tips: Start at a different number (for example 3) if your cover and contents pages should not be counted.
Bottom-centre is the most readable choice for printed documents; bottom-right suits double-sided binding less well, so test a page.
Merge all parts first, then number once so the sequence is continuous.
Need "Page 3 of 20" or dates? Use Header & Footer instead.

faq.q: Can I skip numbering on the cover page?
faq.a: Set the starting number so the count matches your layout, or split off the cover, number the rest and merge again.

faq.q: Will the numbers be editable later?
faq.a: They are drawn into the page content, so they print reliably everywhere; to change them, number the original file again.

deletepages.title: Delete Pages from PDF Online Free – Remove PDF Pages | {brand}
deletepages.desc: Remove unwanted pages from a PDF by tapping thumbnails. Free, no upload, no watermark – a clean new PDF is created on your device.

guide.intro: Blank scans, duplicate pages, outdated appendices or pages with personal details often need to go before you share a document. {brand} shows every page as a thumbnail so you can see exactly what you are removing, and builds the new file locally.
uses: Remove blank pages left by a double-sided scanner.
Drop advert or cover pages from a downloaded report.
Remove pages with personal information before sending a document to a third party.
Trim a long manual down to the sections you actually need.
tips: Zoom in on thumbnails when pages look similar.
Your original file is never modified – keep it until you have checked the result.
To keep a few pages rather than delete many, Extract PDF Pages is quicker.

faq.q: Does deleting pages reduce file size?
faq.a: Usually yes, because the content of removed pages is not copied into the new file. Run Compress PDF afterwards for further savings.

extractpages.title: Extract Pages from PDF Online Free – Save Selected Pages | {brand}
extractpages.desc: Pick the pages you need and save them as a new PDF. Visual page selection, free, unlimited and private – nothing is uploaded.

guide.intro: Often you only need part of a document: one signed page, a single chapter or the pages that mention a project. Extract Pages lets you select those pages visually and save them as a new, smaller PDF without touching the original.
uses: Send only the signature page of a contract back to a client.
Share one chapter of a book or course pack with a study group.
Pull a single statement or invoice out of a combined monthly file.
Collect key slides from a long presentation exported as PDF.
tips: Select pages in any order, then reorder them before clicking Start.
For fixed ranges like 1-5, Split PDF with a page range is faster.
Extracted pages keep their original quality and selectable text.

faq.a: Yes. Tap any combination of pages, for example 2, 7 and 15, and they are saved together in one PDF.

splitbm.title: Split PDF by Bookmarks – Split into Chapters Online Free | {brand}
splitbm.desc: Split a PDF into separate files at each bookmark, such as chapters or sections. Files are named after the bookmarks. Free and private.

guide.intro: Well-structured PDFs – e-books, manuals, standards and annual reports – contain bookmarks (an outline) that mark where each chapter begins. Splitting by bookmarks turns one huge file into tidy chapter files automatically, without you having to look up page numbers.
uses: Break an e-book or textbook into one file per chapter.
Split a technical manual so each team receives only its section.
Separate a combined board pack into individual agenda items.
tips: Open the PDF's bookmark panel first to check the outline exists and is accurate.
Choose top-level bookmarks for chapters, or deeper levels for sections.
No bookmarks? Use Split PDF by Text with a heading like "Chapter".

faq.q: What if my PDF has no bookmarks?
faq.a: Use Split PDF by text (for repeated headings) or Split PDF with page ranges instead.

splitsize.title: Split PDF by File Size – Make PDFs Under an MB Limit | {brand}
splitsize.desc: Split a large PDF into parts that each fit an email or upload size limit (for example 5 MB or 10 MB). Free, no upload, processed locally.

guide.intro: Email providers commonly cap attachments around 20–25 MB, and many upload portals accept far less. Split by Size cuts a big PDF into consecutive parts that each stay under the limit you choose, so you can send it in several messages or uploads.
uses: Send a large scanned contract across several emails.
Upload a long application file to a portal with a per-file size limit.
Share big reports in chat apps that limit file sizes.
tips: Compress the PDF first – you may not need to split at all.
Set the limit slightly below the real cap to allow for email encoding overhead.
A single page larger than the limit is saved on its own; compress that part separately.

faq.q: Why is one part larger than my limit?
faq.a: A single page can be bigger than the limit (for example a high-resolution scan). It is saved as its own file; Compress PDF usually fixes it.

splittext.title: Split PDF by Text – Split at Every Page Containing a Word | {brand}
splittext.desc: Split a PDF wherever a word or phrase appears – such as "Invoice", "Statement" or "Chapter". Free, private, done in your browser.

guide.intro: Batch-printed documents often combine many records into one PDF: hundreds of invoices, payslips or letters. Split by Text starts a new file at every page containing the text you enter, turning one batch into individual documents in seconds.
uses: Split a batch of invoices into one PDF per invoice.
Separate payslips or letters generated in a single mail-merge file.
Break a report at each "Chapter" or "Section" heading.
tips: Use a word that appears only on the first page of each record, such as "Invoice No."
Matching is case-insensitive, so "INVOICE" and "invoice" both work.
The PDF needs a text layer; for scans, run OCR PDF first.

faq.q: Does it work with scanned PDFs?
faq.a: Only if they contain a text layer. Run OCR PDF first, then split by text.

nup.title: N-up PDF – Print Multiple Pages per Sheet Online Free | {brand}
nup.desc: Place 2, 4, 6 or 9 PDF pages on each sheet to save paper and make handouts. Vector quality, A4 or Letter output, free and private.

guide.intro: N-up printing puts several pages on one sheet of paper – perfect for slide handouts, proofreading copies and study notes. {brand} embeds the original pages as vectors, so text stays crisp even when pages are scaled down.
uses: Print lecture slides 4 or 6 to a page as study handouts.
Create compact proof copies of a long document.
Save paper and toner when printing reference material.
tips: 2-up on landscape paper is the most readable for text documents.
6 or 9 per sheet works best for slides with large text.
Choose A4 or Letter to match your printer's paper.

faq.a: No. Pages are embedded as vectors, so they stay sharp at any size.

more: Paper savings
Printing 4 pages per sheet double-sided uses one-eighth of the paper of a single-sided, one-page-per-sheet print. It is ideal for drafts, notes and reference copies.

watermark.title: Add Watermark to PDF Online Free – Text Watermark Any Language | {brand}
watermark.desc: Stamp a text watermark such as CONFIDENTIAL, DRAFT or your company name on PDF pages. Set size, opacity, angle and colour. Free, no upload.

guide.intro: A watermark tells readers a document's status or owner at a glance and discourages unauthorised copying. {brand} adds watermarks in your browser, supports many scripts – Latin, Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari, Thai and more – and never uploads your file.
uses: Mark drafts as DRAFT before circulating them for review.
Label sensitive documents as CONFIDENTIAL.
Brand quotes, portfolios or reports with your company name.
Mark copies of ID documents with "Copy – for rental application only".
tips: Low opacity (15–30%) keeps the document readable.
A 45° diagonal watermark is hardest to crop out.
Combine with Flatten PDF or Rasterize PDF if you want the watermark harder to remove.

faq.a: A text watermark can be removed by determined users with editing software. Rasterizing the PDF afterwards makes removal much harder.

headerfooter.title: Add Header and Footer to PDF Online Free – Page X of Y, Date | {brand}
headerfooter.desc: Add headers and footers with page numbers, totals, dates and file names to every PDF page. Free, private, no watermark.

guide.intro: Headers and footers give documents a professional finish and context on every page: the document title, "Page 3 of 12", a date or a confidentiality line. {brand} supports placeholders, so one setting produces the right text for each page.
uses: Add "Page {page} of {total}" to reports and proposals.
Put the company name and "Confidential" on every page.
Stamp the print date on records and audit documents.
Label pages of an exhibit with the file name.
tips: Placeholders: {page}, {total}, {date} and {file}.
Keep headers short so they do not overlap page content.
For legal numbering across many files, use Bates Numbering.

faq.q: Can I use different text on the left, centre and right?
faq.a: Yes, set each position separately in the options.

more: Professional documents
Consistent headers and footers with titles, dates and page numbers make reports, proposals and legal documents easier to navigate and reference.

bates.title: Bates Numbering PDF Online Free – Legal Document Numbering | {brand}
bates.desc: Apply sequential Bates numbers (prefix, digits, suffix) across multiple PDFs for legal discovery and records. Free, private, no upload.

guide.intro: Bates numbering gives every page in a set of documents a unique, sequential identifier, such as ABC000001 – a standard in litigation, discovery and compliance work. Because {brand} runs locally, privileged and confidential documents are never sent to a third-party server.
uses: Number documents for legal discovery or disclosure.
Label pages of evidence bundles and exhibits.
Track pages in audit, insurance or compliance submissions.
tips: Choose enough digits for the whole production (6 digits covers up to 999,999 pages).
Order files correctly before starting; numbering continues from one file to the next.
Use a matter-specific prefix to avoid confusion between cases.

faq.a: Yes. Numbers continue from one file to the next in the order shown.

more: Bates number format

A typical Bates number combines a prefix (often a case or party code), a zero-padded sequence and optional suffix, for example SMITH-000123. Positioning in the bottom-right corner is a common convention.

crop.title: Crop PDF Online Free – Trim PDF Margins | {brand}
crop.desc: Crop PDF pages by exact millimetres to remove white margins or focus on content. All pages or selected pages. Free and private.

guide.intro: Scanned pages and exported slides often have wide margins or unwanted borders. Cropping trims the visible page area, making documents easier to read on phones and e-readers and tidier when printed.
uses: Remove wide white margins for easier reading on a phone or tablet.
Cut off scanner borders and shadows.
Focus on a chart or figure for a presentation.
tips: Measure on one page and apply to all if pages share the same layout.
Cropping hides content but does not delete it – use Redact PDF for sensitive content.
After cropping, Change Page Size can fit content back to A4 or Letter.

faq.a: No. It is hidden outside the new page box. Use Redact PDF to permanently remove sensitive content.

more: Crop for e-readers
Removing wide margins makes the text larger on small screens, which is especially useful for academic papers and scanned books read on phones, tablets and e-readers.

findreplace.title: Find and Replace Text in PDF Online Free | {brand}
findreplace.desc: Find a word or phrase in a PDF and replace it with new text, directly in your browser. Free, no upload, no sign-up.

guide.intro: Spotted a misspelled name, an outdated date or an old price in a PDF? Find & Replace locates every occurrence and writes your new text in its place – useful when you no longer have the original Word or design file.
uses: Fix a typo in a name or address.
Update a date, price or version number across a document.
Replace an old company name after a rebrand.
tips: Works on PDFs with a text layer; scans need OCR first.
Keep replacement text a similar length so it fits the space.
If the old text must be removed for confidentiality, use Redact PDF.

faq.q: Is the old text really gone?
faq.a: The old text is removed from the page content and the new text is drawn in the same font, size and colour where possible.

metadata.title: Edit PDF Metadata Online Free – Title, Author, Keywords | {brand}
metadata.desc: View and edit PDF title, author, subject and keywords, or remove them. Free, private, done in your browser.

guide.intro: PDF metadata is the hidden information stored in a file: title, author, subject, keywords, the creating software and dates. A proper title shows in browser tabs and search results, while stale author names can leak information you did not mean to share.
uses: Set a descriptive title before publishing a PDF on your website.
Correct the author name on documents created from a template.
Add keywords to help document management systems find files.
tips: The Title field is what browsers show in the tab – make it meaningful.
To remove everything quickly, use Remove PDF Metadata.

faq.q: Does metadata affect SEO for PDFs?
faq.a: Search engines can use the PDF title, so a clear, accurate title helps people find and recognise your document.

more: Professional publishing
A clear title, author and subject make PDFs look professional in browser tabs, document management systems and search results. Update metadata before publishing whitepapers, reports and ebooks.

flatten.title: Flatten PDF Online Free – Make Form Fields Non-Editable | {brand}
flatten.desc: Flatten fillable PDF forms and annotations so values can no longer be changed, or flatten every page into an image. Free and private.

guide.intro: When you send a completed form, the recipient can usually still edit its fields. Flattening merges field values and annotations into the page so the form looks the same everywhere and cannot be casually changed.
uses: Lock a completed application or tax form before submitting it.
Make sure comments and stamps display in every viewer.
Fix forms whose fields show blank on phones or in some printers.
tips: Use "Form fields only" to keep text selectable.
"Everything" mode turns pages into images – stronger, but text cannot be selected.
Keep an unflattened copy in case you need to edit later.

faq.a: Yes in Form fields only mode. Everything mode converts pages to images.

more: Why flatten forms
Interactive form fields can display differently between viewers and can be edited after you submit them. Flattening locks the values into the page so what you send is exactly what the recipient sees.

redact.title: Redact PDF Online Free – Permanently Black Out Text | {brand}
redact.desc: Permanently redact words and areas in a PDF. Redacted pages are rebuilt so hidden text cannot be copied or recovered. Free, private.

guide.intro: Drawing a black box over text in many editors leaves the text underneath – anyone can copy it out. True redaction removes it. {brand} rebuilds every redacted page so the hidden content is gone, and because it runs locally, the sensitive document never leaves your device.
uses: Hide account numbers, ID numbers and signatures before sharing.
Remove personal data from documents released under privacy or freedom-of-information requests.
Black out client names in case studies or court filings.
tips: Search for a word to redact every occurrence at once, then add boxes for images or signatures.
Check the result by trying to select and copy text in the redacted areas.
Also run Remove PDF Metadata – author names and titles can reveal information.

faq.a: No. Every page with a redaction is rebuilt as an image with the areas blacked out, so the underlying text is gone. Other pages are kept unchanged.

compare.title: Compare PDF Online Free – Find Differences Between Two PDFs | {brand}
compare.desc: Compare two PDF versions and highlight added, removed and changed text side by side. Free, private, no upload.

guide.intro: Contract revisions, policy updates and new document versions often arrive without tracked changes. Compare PDF shows exactly which words were added, deleted or changed between two versions, so nothing slips through.
uses: Check what changed between two versions of a contract.
Review edits to terms and conditions or policies.
Verify that a final print file matches the approved proof.
tips: Put the older version first so additions and removals read naturally.
Scanned PDFs need OCR before their text can be compared.

faq.q: Does it compare images and layout?
faq.a: This version compares text. Visual comparison is planned.

more: When to compare PDFs
Use Compare PDF whenever you receive a “final” version of a contract, policy, specification or academic paper. Small changes in numbers, dates or liability clauses are easy to miss when reading.
Reading the results
Removed text is marked in one colour and added text in another, side by side, so you can review each change and ask about anything unexpected before signing.

grayscale.title: Grayscale PDF Online Free – Convert Color PDF to Black and White | {brand}
grayscale.desc: Convert a colour PDF to grayscale to save ink and toner or meet black-and-white submission rules. Free, private, done in your browser.

guide.intro: Printing colour documents on a black-and-white printer can make text look faint, and colour ink is expensive. Converting to grayscale shows exactly how the document will print and can cut costs.
uses: Save colour ink when printing long documents at home or the office.
Meet submission rules that require black-and-white documents.
Preview how charts and photos will look on a monochrome printer.
tips: Check charts after conversion – colours that differ only in hue may look identical in grey.
Compress PDF afterwards for an even smaller file.

faq.a: No, pages are converted to grayscale images, so text is not selectable afterwards. Run OCR PDF if you need searchable text.

more: Ink and toner savings
Colour cartridges are expensive and many offices default to black-and-white printing. Converting first lets you check readability of charts and highlights before printing, avoiding wasted pages.
Smaller files too
Colour images contain three channels of information; grayscale needs only one, so converting can also reduce file size for image-heavy documents.

deskew.title: Deskew PDF Online Free – Straighten Scanned Pages | {brand}
deskew.desc: Automatically detect and straighten tilted pages in scanned PDFs. Free, private, processed in your browser.

Practical examples

A 500 g pack is 17.6 oz; a 2 kg bag of flour is 4.4 lb; 80 kg body weight is 12 st 8 lb. When shipping parcels, carriers often round up to the next whole kilogram or pound, so convert before you buy postage.
Cooking with weights
Weighing ingredients is more accurate than using cups. Many US recipes give ounces and pounds; converting to grams lets you use a kitchen scale set to metric for consistent results.

guide.intro: Switch between Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin for weather, cooking, science or health.
uses: Understand weather forecasts abroad.
Convert oven temperatures in recipes.
Convert for science homework.
tips: Water freezes at 0 °C (32 °F) and boils at 100 °C (212 °F).

faq.a: No. 0 K is absolute zero, the lowest possible temperature.

more: Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin explained

Celsius is based on water freezing at 0° and boiling at 100°. Fahrenheit, used in the US, puts those points at 32° and 212°. Kelvin is the scientific absolute scale: 0 K is absolute zero, and one kelvin is the same size as one degree Celsius, so you simply add 273.15.
Common conversions
Oven: 200 °C ≈ 392 °F. Fever: 38 °C = 100.4 °F. Freezer: −18 °C ≈ 0 °F. Room temperature in science is often 298.15 K (25 °C). Note that −40 is the same in both Celsius and Fahrenheit.
Temperature in cooking

European and many international recipes give oven temperatures in Celsius, US recipes in Fahrenheit, and fan ovens usually need about 20 °C (35 °F) less than conventional ovens. Converting carefully prevents burnt or undercooked dishes.

guide.intro: Convert land and floor areas between square metres, square feet, acres, hectares and more – useful for property, farming and construction.
uses: Compare property sizes between countries.
Convert floor plans from sq ft to m².
Calculate land in acres or hectares.
tips: 1 hectare = 10,000 m² ≈ 2.471 acres.

faq.a: Square metres, square feet, acres, hectares and several regional land units.

faq.q: How many square feet are in a square metre?
faq.a: About 10.764.

more: Area units for property and land

Property listings use square metres in most of the world and square feet in the US, UK (partly), Canada and parts of Asia. Agricultural land is usually measured in hectares or acres. Regional units such as the cent and ground remain common in some local land records, so they are included too.
Useful equivalents
1 m² = 10.7639 sq ft. 1 acre = 4,046.86 m² = 43,560 sq ft. 1 hectare = 10,000 m² = 2.471 acres. 1 km² = 100 hectares. A typical football pitch is about 0.7 hectares (1.75 acres).

guide.intro: Storage sizes come in decimal (MB, GB) and binary (MiB, GiB) units, which is why a "1 TB" drive shows less space on your computer. Convert between them and network speeds.
uses: Understand drive capacities.
Estimate download times from Mbit/s speeds.
Check file sizes against upload limits.
tips: 1 GB = 1,000 MB, but 1 GiB = 1,024 MiB.
8 bits = 1 byte.

faq.q: Why does my drive show less space?
faq.a: Manufacturers use decimal units while many operating systems display binary units.

faq.q: Is a megabit the same as a megabyte?
faq.a: No. One byte is 8 bits, so 1 MB = 8 Mbit.

more: Decimal vs binary units

Storage makers use decimal prefixes (1 GB = 1,000,000,000 bytes), while Windows and some tools show binary values (1 GiB = 1,073,741,824 bytes). That is why a “1 TB” drive shows about 931 GB in Windows – nothing is missing.
Bits, bytes and internet speed

Internet speeds are quoted in megabits per second (Mbit/s), file sizes in megabytes (MB). Divide by 8: a 100 Mbit/s connection downloads about 12.5 MB per second in ideal conditions, so a 1 GB file takes around 80 seconds.

guide.intro: Convert centimetres to inches for clothing sizes, screens, paper and craft projects.
uses: Compare clothing or shoe measurements.
Convert screen and frame sizes.
Follow sewing or craft patterns.
tips: 1 in = 2.54 cm exactly.

faq.q: How do I convert cm to inches?
faq.a: Divide centimetres by 2.54.

faq.q: How many cm are in a foot?
faq.a: One foot is exactly 30.48 cm.

more: Where the inch is still used

Even in metric countries, inches appear on TV and monitor sizes, phone screens, bicycle wheels, pipe fittings and denim waist sizes. Paper sizes differ too: A4 is 21 × 29.7 cm (8.27 × 11.69 in) while US Letter is 8.5 × 11 in (21.59 × 27.94 cm).
Quick estimates
Divide by 2.5 for a fast estimate, then adjust slightly up: 30 cm ≈ 11.8 in, 50 cm ≈ 19.7 in, 100 cm ≈ 39.4 in. For height, 170 cm is 5 ft 7 in and 180 cm is 5 ft 11 in.
Clothing and shoe sizes

Waist and inseam sizes for jeans are given in inches in many countries, while body measurements on size charts are often in centimetres. Measure in either unit and convert to choose the right size when shopping internationally.

guide.intro: Convert kilograms to pounds for fitness, travel luggage, shipping and recipes.
uses: Check gym weights and body weight.
Convert luggage allowances.
Calculate shipping weights.

faq.q: How many pounds are in a kilogram?
faq.a: 1 kg equals about 2.20462 lb.

faq.q: How do I convert pounds to kilograms?
faq.a: Divide pounds by 2.20462, or multiply by 0.45359237.

more: Kilograms vs pounds: where each is used

The kilogram is the SI unit of mass and is used for everyday weights in almost every country. The pound (avoirdupois) is common in the United States and is still used informally in the United Kingdom, often together with stone for body weight. Since 1959 the pound has been defined exactly as 0.45359237 kg, so conversions are precise rather than approximate.
Quick mental maths

To estimate pounds, double the kilograms and add 10%: 70 kg × 2 = 140, plus 14 gives about 154 lb (exact: 154.32 lb). To go the other way, halve the pounds and subtract 10%: 200 lb ÷ 2 = 100, minus 10 gives about 90 kg (exact: 90.72 kg). For airline baggage, 23 kg is about 50.7 lb and 32 kg is about 70.5 lb – the two most common checked-bag limits.

guide.intro: Convert Celsius to Fahrenheit for weather, cooking and health – essential when travelling or using recipes from the US.
uses: Understand US weather forecasts.
Convert oven temperatures.
Check body temperature readings.
tips: Quick estimate: double °C and add 30.

faq.q: How do I convert Fahrenheit to Celsius?

more: Where Fahrenheit is still used

Most of the world measures temperature in Celsius, but the United States, some Caribbean nations and a few Pacific territories still use Fahrenheit for weather, cooking and medicine. If you read US recipes, weather apps or medical advice, converting quickly avoids mistakes – especially with oven temperatures.
Handy reference points

0 °C = 32 °F (freezing), 20 °C = 68 °F (room temperature), 37 °C = 98.6 °F (normal body temperature), 100 °C = 212 °F (boiling at sea level), and 180 °C ≈ 356 °F, the most common oven setting. The quick estimate “double it and add 30” is accurate within a few degrees for everyday weather.
Body temperature
A normal body temperature is around 36.5–37.5 °C (97.7–99.5 °F). A fever is generally considered 38 °C (100.4 °F) or higher.

guide.intro: Lakh and crore are number units used in South Asian business news and finance. This converter translates them into the international million and billion system.
uses: Understand figures in South Asian business news.
Convert financial reports for international readers.
tips: 1 lakh = 100,000; 1 crore = 10 million.

faq.q: How many lakh are in a million?
faq.a: 1 million = 10 lakh.

faq.q: How many crore are in a billion?
faq.a: 1 billion = 100 crore.

more: How the two numbering systems group digits

The international system groups digits in thousands: 1,000,000 is one million. The South Asian system groups the first three digits and then pairs: 10,00,000 is ten lakh – the same number. Business news, salaries and property prices in South Asia are often quoted in lakh and crore, so international readers need a quick translation.
Key equivalents
1 lakh = 100,000 (one hundred thousand). 10 lakh = 1 million. 1 crore = 10 million. 100 crore = 1 billion. So a figure of 250 crore equals 2.5 billion.
Reading financial reports
Annual reports and news from South Asia often state revenue in crore. Converting to million or billion makes figures directly comparable with international companies and currencies.

uses: Schedule international meetings and webinars.
Plan calls with remote colleagues or clients.
Check flight arrival times.
tips: Daylight saving dates differ between the US, Europe and the southern hemisphere – always check the date.

faq.a: Yes, automatically, based on the selected date.

faq.q: Where does the time zone data come from?
faq.a: Your browser's built-in IANA time zone database, updated with your browser.

more: How time zones and daylight saving work

There are more than 38 local time offsets in use, including half-hour and 45-minute zones such as India (UTC+05:30) and Nepal (UTC+05:45). Daylight saving is observed in North America, most of Europe and parts of Australia and South America – on different dates – while most of Asia and Africa do not change clocks.
Tips for international scheduling

Choose cities rather than abbreviations, because “CST” can mean US Central, China or Cuba Standard Time. Note when Europe and the US change clocks on different weekends in March and October/November: for a week or two the usual gap between London and New York shrinks by an hour.

guide.intro: Convert India Standard Time to US Eastern Time, accounting for daylight saving in the US.
uses: Schedule calls between India and the US East Coast.
tips: The difference is 9h30 in winter (EST) and 10h30 in summer (EDT).

faq.a: Yes, based on the date you choose.

faq.q: What is the time difference now?
faq.a: It is 9h30 during US daylight saving time and 10h30 otherwise.

more: Daylight saving and the time difference

India Standard Time is UTC+05:30 all year. US Eastern Time is UTC−5 (EST) in winter and UTC−4 (EDT) from the second Sunday in March to the first Sunday in November. That makes India 10 h 30 min ahead in winter and 9 h 30 min ahead in summer.
Scheduling tips

Overlap is short: 8:00–10:00 AM in New York is 6:30–8:30 PM (summer) or 5:30–7:30 PM (winter) in India. Put both local times in every invitation and let calendar apps convert automatically to avoid missed calls.
Business hours overlap
With a 9h30–10h30 gap, the working days in India and the US East Coast barely overlap. Most teams meet in the US morning, which is India's evening, or use asynchronous updates.

guide.intro: Convert India Standard Time to US Pacific Time with daylight saving handled automatically.
uses: Schedule calls between India and the US West Coast.
tips: The difference is 13h30 (PST) or 12h30 (PDT).

faq.a: Yes. The date you choose determines whether PST or PDT applies.
Often yes – India is ahead, so evening in California is already the next morning in India.

more: Why the gap changes during the year

India keeps UTC+05:30 all year, but the US West Coast switches between Pacific Standard Time (UTC−8) and Pacific Daylight Time (UTC−7). Daylight saving starts on the second Sunday of March and ends on the first Sunday of November, so the difference is 13 hours 30 minutes in winter and 12 hours 30 minutes in summer.
Finding a good meeting slot

A 9:00 AM meeting in California is 9:30 PM or 10:30 PM in India, while 8:00 AM in India is the previous evening on the West Coast. Many distributed teams use early-morning Pacific / late-evening India slots. Always include both times and the date in invitations, because the calendar day often differs.

guide.intro: Convert UTC/GMT to India Standard Time (UTC+05:30) – useful for server logs, flights and events.
uses: Read server logs in local time.
Convert event times announced in UTC.
tips: India does not use daylight saving.

faq.a: IST is UTC+05:30 all year; India does not observe daylight saving.

faq.q: Is GMT the same as UTC?
faq.a: For everyday purposes yes; technically UTC is the precise atomic-clock standard.

more: What UTC is and why it matters

Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) is the global reference time used by aviation, servers, satellites and international events. GMT is often used as a synonym in everyday speech. Because UTC never changes for daylight saving, it is the safest way to record timestamps in logs, databases and APIs.
Reading timestamps correctly

ISO 8601 timestamps ending in “Z” (for example 2026-03-01T14:00:00Z) are in UTC. Add 5 hours 30 minutes to get India Standard Time: 14:00 UTC is 19:30 IST. When a timestamp has an explicit offset like +05:30 it is already local and needs no conversion.
Converting the other way
To convert IST to UTC, subtract 5 hours 30 minutes: 09:00 IST is 03:30 UTC. Remember that the date can change around midnight.
